bull.b: Exceptional payment-volume growth demonstrates strong merchant adoption and expanding transaction activity across dLocal’s emerging-market network. The raised full-year outlook reinforces that momentum is expected to persist, supporting revenue growth and operating leverage over the next several quarters.

Very high revenue and payment-volume retention indicate that existing merchants are increasing their use of dLocal’s platform rather than merely being replaced by new customers. This deepening engagement can create durable volume growth, improve customer economics, and strengthen competitive positioning.

Minimal leverage gives dLocal substantial financial flexibility to invest in product expansion, technology, and market growth without relying heavily on debt financing. Strong returns on equity also indicate effective capital use, supporting resilience if operating conditions become less favorable.

bear.b: The multi-year decline in gross and net margins shows that rapid growth has not translated fully into sustained profitability expansion. If the lower margin profile persists, dLocal may have less earnings conversion from future payment volume and reduced flexibility to absorb cost or pricing pressures.

Lower take rates can limit revenue growth even when payment volume expands rapidly, particularly as local-to-local flows, payouts, and large merchant relationships become a greater share of activity. Persistent mix pressure could therefore reduce monetization and constrain operating leverage.

Recent cash generation is strong and closely tracks earnings, but the negative operating and free cash flow recorded in 2024 demonstrates that conversion can fluctuate materially. Such volatility may complicate investment planning and make internally funded growth less predictable across periods.
